correctness.rationale: Lucas identifies each row's support as a radix digit box. Independently, split a row n=a p^(r-1)+t into a+1 increasing copies of the support at t, shifted by successive multiples of p^(r-1). The within-copy gaps contribute A times the depth-(r-1) pooled histogram after summing over a; the a boundary gaps all equal p^(r-1)-t because each lower support begins at 0 and ends at t. Varying t covers each size 1 through p^(r-1) once and summing a gives B for each. Thus the depth-r histogram is A times the preceding one plus that flat contribution, starting from an empty depth-0 histogram. This verifies the full formula, including p=2, r=1 and the sharp cutoff. Row support sizes sum to A^r, and removing one endpoint per row counts A^r-p^r pairs; their lengths telescope to the row indices, proving the finite mean. The normalized limit is a probability law: it mixes the discrete uniforms on 1,...,p^i with weights (B/A)(p/A)^i, summing to one since A-p=B. The shell of p^i-p^(i-1) points gives the stated tail and a geometric s-moment term of order (p^(s+1)/A)^i, including divergence at equality. The moment claim concerns nonnegative orders. Independent direct binomial-coefficient enumeration agreed on six prime/depth cases; this is finite corroboration only, distinct from the supplied additive Pascal-row checker and its recorded CHECK_OK.
residual_risks: No conclusions for different row weightings, gaps joining different rows, or higher prime-power nondivisibility thresholds.

value.rationale: Within-row nearest-neighbor gaps distinguish a fractal's spacing from its support size and its longest surviving block. The exact finite spectrum for every prime and depth resolves every gap size under a natural pair-weighted ensemble; the exact normalized tail further explains why the limiting mean diverges even though every finite mean exists. The boundary-counting argument is elementary but the statistic and its heavy-tail cutoff are usable in studies of the Pascal support.
residual_risks: This is a pooled one-gap law, not a description of correlations between consecutive gaps or a claim about a stationary infinite process.
